newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer upbeat, to stress acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Placer upbeat, to stress acquisitions.

text.p: Gold producer Placer Dome Inc gave an upbeat assessment Thursday of its prospects and said it was giving higher priority to acquisitions.

In a conference call with investment analysts, Chief Executive John Willson said the year was unfolding as the company had hoped with the start of "a significant improvement in our production and cost profile that would have a very strong impact on our results starting in 1998."

"Our operating performance has been much stronger this year. Gold production is increasing as expected and costs are coming down. Furthermore new mines are exceeding expectations," he said, according to a text of his remarks released by the company.
He noted that Placer had increased its gold production forecast for the year by 100,000 ounces to 2.4 million.
Placer on Tuesday reported that it turned a second quarter profit of US$19 million, up from a US$32 million loss a year earlier.
Willson also said the company had "taken steps to give acquisitions a higher priority." These included a reorganization of its offices and top executives.
"...We recognize that successful acquisitions are essential to augment the reserves we will find through exploration," Willson said.
He told the call that Placer was considering a number of opportunities but gave no details, a company spokesman said.

While the recent sharp drop in the gold price has been disappointing to the company, it provides a window of opportunity for acquisitions. Placer will stress acquisitions of high-quality projects that offer prospects of long-life mines, low costs and large reserves, the spokesman said.
Willson told the call that the partners in the Las Cristinas gold mine project in Venezuela hoped to begin construction of a base camp there in a "matter of months," the spokesman said.
A legal dispute with Crystallex International Corp over ownership has delayed the project, but Placer is confident enough in its legal position to consider a production decision, he said.
Construction of the mine will take two years and production was originally scheduled to begin in early 1999.

Placer said its operating cash flows were strong and increasing, enabling it to maintain current levels of exploration spending and to meet planned capital expenditures and debt repayment. Willson described the company's financial condition as excellent despite the slumping gold price.

Thanks to hedging, Placer expects to realize an average gold price in 1997 of US$360 to US$370 an ounce if spot prices remain roughly constant. Over the next four years it would expect to realize US$475 an ounce on a third of its total production and the value of its hedge position at the end of the second quarter was US$400 million.
Placer is pleased with the performance of its new Pipeline and Musselwhite mines.
